Part 1 · Solution paths

Every path, so you can decide

Each problem has two or more possible solution paths, each with pros, drawbacks, who gains, who loses, how to mend the losers, and where it has been tried. Many paths create new problems, which have their own subpaths. Nothing here is chosen yet.

Two sets of picks are built out as full plans: the current draft, a Germany-style hybrid (plan), and the earlier single-payer draft, kept as an alternative (plan, path). Compare them on Compare approaches.

Compare against changing nothing
Every problem in today's system also has a “Keep current law” option, and every path is labeled by how much it changes today's system. Compare approaches puts keeping current law, minor changes, bigger changes that keep today's insurers, a universal multi-payer system, the earlier single-payer draft, and the current draft (a Germany-style hybrid) side by side.
How to read the relationships
  • Addresses / also helps: problems the path fixes (479 links in total across paths).
  • Creates or worsens: new problems the path causes. Expand “creates” below to see the subpaths that answer them.
  • Requires: another path that must also be chosen.
  • Conflicts (12 pairs): choosing one rules out the other. Works well with (58 pairs): natural combinations.
